title: the incredible adventures of van helsing
text: The incredible Adventures of Van Helsing ( an all dlc version review ) This game offers you a choice of 3 different classes, each with a very solid selection of skills, first being a hunter which can actually be built in 3 different ways entirely on its own, or hybridized to your hearts content, having melee, ranged ( pistols and rifles ) and occult ( magic ) skills at his disposal. The second class is the Thaumaturge who is a pure spellcaster with plethora of skills at his disposal both offensive and control/support, all having their specific use, and the final class is a unique Arcane mechanic, having mine and grenade skills at his disposal, as well as gadgets and turrets. It is a very well done, unique and incredibly refreshing setting that this game is taking place in, there are no dwarves, no elfs, no typical fantasy arpg of which there is 16874 on the market and all look the same in the end. The game is set in a beautiful gothic noir setting with mythical, as well as mechanical creatures to be fought, and with exciting places to explore. Speaking about the monsters - They are designed well and look unique, there is swarms of them, so there is always alot of action, and thus, there is also tons of actually good loot, what more could you wish for, right? Speaking of loot, the itemization in this game is very well done. There is very typical item system of normal, magic, rare ( thus far the exact same as diablo II, including colors ) and finally epic and set items, which all have functionality like stat comparison to your equipped item, comparison to your followers equipped items ( more on that in a bit ) etc, a bit of a downside perhaps could be  that later on in the game, you may start getting lost in the constant stat comparations, because in this game it is fairly usual to be swapping items for new ones often. And what deserves a mention as well is that the devs were not afraid to actually let you drop or be rewarded with the epic items, one of my dislikes about other recent Arpg's is that you basically never get to see any of the highest tier items unless you farm for them for ages or play advanced game modes. This brings me to quest rewards, and money, since they go hand in hand. This is another area this game excels at. You get very, very good rewards even for sidequests you'd think were meaningless or not worth to bother with, being used to that from other, maybe even most rpg's. But in here, you are always rewarded with a rare item, sometimes in fact a unique ( epic ) one, with skill or stat points ( sometimes for you, sometimes for your follower ), and a decent sum of money, which are useful for quite alot of things as well. The experience reward for quests could I thought be higher, but then again, I reached the max level just playing the game normally, so there was no need for it then. And regarding money, another often overlooked area in other games, in here, you can then spend them upgrading your weapons, reseting your stat or skill points ( no other limits  for that then your money, awesome! ), gambling for items, and later on even improving the hideout where your character interacts with friendly npc's. Remember the mention of a follower? You indeed have one, bound to you by the storyline, and when I saw this, I was not happy about that, having experiences from most other games where followers are just constantly dead and useless. Not so in here, your follower, a ghost woman called Katarina has her own level progression with attribute points and 2 skill trees, one of which improves you by her actions/simply being with you, and the other purely improving her alone. This leaves incredible versatility and usefulness to her because you are completely free to make her an uberpowerful tank if you need it, and if it so happens she'd die, you can actually enable her to explode on death, usually clearing the whole mob of enemies that was attacking her. If you are melee, you are in turn completely free to make her your ranged support, or even if you so wish, to leave her out of the battle and just give you a permanent 10% dmg reduction. Furthermore, you could also tell her which items she would pick up ( if any ) and in which way should she attack your enemies, I wouldnt ask for more. Along Katarinas level up progression, and yours, which of course also lets you assign the typical attribute and skill points, there is more for your character than that. Much more. Along the regular skill tree ( or trees, for the Hunter class ), you also get an entire additional passive skill tree, which is in part unique and partially shared to/by all the classes, where you could choose from a number of passive skills two that you want to have active at all times. Want dmg reduction? Its there, want to heal Katarina with your attacks? Sure, and so much more. And thats still not all. There is an additional skill tree called "tricks" which you can also invest skill points, which are very useful active abilities like stopping the time, making 2 more katarinas temporarily to help you, or my spellcasters favourite, being able to burn all your mana for a massive explosion around him. Since the Thaumaturgist's spells are mainly focused on damage over time ( DoT ), this is a great tool to have for burst damage. Thought thats all? Nope, still not yet, because there are additionally perks too.. You get those for killing big bosses and in general unusual monsters like veterans and champions, and they furthermore permanently improve your character to the point where you can choose to be impossible to be stopped in your tracks, or to not die when killed, and merely become incorporeal for several seconds. Now thats what I call a character progression, and to my best knowledge, I can honestly say it is unparalleled by any other single player Arpg's out there. The game as it is at the moment is imo a truly great experience free of any glitches or bugs, after being patched multiple times, which is incredibly impressive for a game studio so small that the final credits only rolled for about 1 single minute, no exaggeration. The game has very professional voice acting, as well as enjoyable music which deserves a mention, and the game is also full of very funny references to all kinds of things, including other games, of the same genre or otherwise, sometimes fairly hidden, sometimes very obvious. Some games may try to make jokes which dont fit in it, or some games just go full "funny" all the way, but what is impressive  about this game is that it manages to have an interesting, serious, believable world and atmosphere, and yet, effortlessly manages to include funny references in it that just make you smile.. The games lenght is very solid 18 hours for one playthrough which is great, considering there are scenario mode and a game+ mode available as well, so replayability is great. Sumarry: An amazing action rpg game that has been a ton of pure fun thanks to its for a single player rpg unrivaled character development options, unique setting, fluent game mechanics that are clear and work exactly as youd expect at all times, and thanks to the constant rewards the game gives you which will never make you leave it for long until youve seen it all. And that would take at least a while. Highly recommended to get, the developers really deserve to be rewarded for a game this polished and with this many gameplay features. Rating: 89/100 Pros: Unique setting Character development Useful follower Item types, customization options Npc functionalities Game's lasting appeal Smart, funny references Made by a very small team, yet feeling as an AAA title for Cons: Recycling of enemies in some levels Sometimes can become messy with swarms of enemies around Stat comparing may feel a bit confusing

text: This for me was one of the highligts of the last sale, very competently done, good dialogue, very impressive and well detailed backdrops, a decent variety of things to kill and a competently done Diablo 2-esque control and combat system. The main star of the show in this game for me is the setting, a steampunk inspired continuation of the story of Van Helsing. There is even a little off colour humour from your companion, and this is even played just right so it doesn't become overbearing. Another pleasant feature is the depth of the world, there's loads of little side missions you can do that you discover during your travels, they don't affect the main plot but they add so much flavour to the world. The game does have its downsides however, it can vary greatly in difficulty in places, varying from very, very easy to punishingly difficult, this isn't too much of a problem though and can be easily overlooked. There is also a tower defence section, while optional I really don't like tower defence and found it kind of tacked on and unnecessary. Yes it's all been done before but does that make it any less fun? I don't think so, I'd give it a 8/10

text: One of my favorite games, and still in alpha. Well-polished controls and menus/submenus, beautiful graphics throughout, really impressive sounds that immerse you in the environment, and fairly unforgiving gameplay.  I guess you could call this somewhat Rogue-like, in that there's an RPG element (skill progression) and permadeath.  Resources are procedurally generated, though environments are fixed. I especially love how few instructions there are to learn how to play the game--everything requires exploration and experimentation, but not at all in a frustrating way.  Learning to play the game is part of the game--but I doubt it will ever get easy no matter what.  Hunting is really difficult, and you're always on the verge of freezing or starving.  I love it!

text: This game starts you off by punching you in the face, stabbing you in the stomach, and kicking you in the teeth.  If you survive the first week, odds are good you'll go the distance and survive forever until you get bored and start over.  You start off grossly underdressed and underequipped, and the first few days are touch and go.  Maybe you'll find some better clothes before the cold kills you. Maybe you'll evade the wolves long enough to acquire a decent weapon.  If you can tough it out, you'll become the predator, strolling around proudly wearing the wolfskin coat, deer hide boots and pants, and rabbitskin mitts.  If you're particularly savvy with your rifle and flare gun, you'll even manage to sleep soundly in a handmade bearskin bedroll.  Whether you die poorly to the elements, die like a warrior in battle, or survive as a master of your domain, this game will challenge even the most veteran players, while remaining playable even to a novice. My only gripe with the game is that if you do manage to survive for an extended period of time--namely if you manage to acquire the 200 day achievement...it's still friggen winter.  Seriously, are we in an ice age now?  I get it, it's northern Canada, but still.  After 200 days you'd think you might start to see some vestiges of summer.  But nope, always winter.  C'est la vie. Still worth it.

text: I rarely write reviews, but I have enjoyed this game so much I felt the developers deserve it. I started out in this game with little clothes, in a valley someplace in a fridgid environment, no idea of directions and starting to freeze immediately. It was frightening. Starving, no water, and not realizing how fast I could catch hypothermia and die were constant companions. The game does a great job of immersion and I must admit I was sucked into it for almost 40 hours within a few says before I realized how much I was playing it. Early game the worst part was the freezing, getting caught in a blizzard or high winds with little protection, getting lost and not knowing where my basecamp was, even what a basecamp was. I got lost constantly, trying to remember landmarks but when a snowstorm comes up its so easy to get lost. No water...dehydrated....weak...starving...calories burn faster the colder it is...didnt know that....so cold. That moment when I spot a deer carcass..my heart jumps and I am so hopeful, only to find out it is frozen and I am unable to harvest it with my bare hands. I think I died from hypothermia that night. Early game I died quite a bit, my first 5 games often dying within the first 48 hours. Then figuring out how to balance my time, because originally I was pretty frantic and not knowing what to do to survive. One minute I would be gathering wood, next getting dehydrated because I ran out of drink and not knowing how to melt snow. Starving...getting attacked by wolves...really scary stuff. I am now past day 50. I have figured out how to balance my time, and to plan my days out in advance. Have killed wolves, deer, have made clothing from their hides which allows me to manage the cold quite well, even in the worst storms. There is no longer constant terror as a companion, but there is no time to sit on my laurels, firewood, food, water, repairs to equipment does not allow a life of leisure. Overall, I really recommend buying this game. It is worth every penny. Last comment...screw bears in general. Getting mauled sucks. Good luck out there.

text: UPDATED:  I changed my review to recommended since the sandbox mode is fantastic and well worth the price if you enjoy this kind of game. I've been playing this game for a couple years now through its development in sandbox mode and have really enjoyed it.  Yes, some of the mechanics are a bit crude and yes, it can be quite tedious at times - but I like the simplicity.  I also like that it doesn't fetishize guns like a lot of other survival games.  I'm also from, and live on, the island where the game is developed (and takes place... kind of...), and I just really wanted it to turn into something great.  It has a fantastic foundation. Throughout the past couple years, I've always been impressed that it has had constant updates that have made huge improvements to gameplay, ui, and content.  However, within the past year I guess resources have been shifted to story mode and some of the frustrating issues of the game have just... remained.  In sandbox mode, as you progress from surviving a couple of days to multiple weeks, these issues really start to stand out. The meat issue.  A deer will yeild 10kg (22lbs) of meat.  Okay - that's reasonable.  But buddy will gobble that away in just two days.  I mean, come on.  Thats like 15,000 calories - it should last at least a week.  If you could store things outside in the cold... You can't store food in the cold (maybe they've fixed this now?).  That's a pretty fundamental aspect of wilderness survival, especially long-term.  There should be a robust system for caching food - hangs, boxes, etc.  If you can't stockpile, then what's even the point? Wolves.  I get it - geomagnetic blah, blah, blah.  They're all hopped up on goofballs and want to kill everything.  But if they're going to be such a central part of the game, then maybe don't make them so one-dimensional.  Vary their behaviour or something... That's one of the most terrifying and dangerous things about animals in the wild - they're unpredictable. These things are just robots.  They get boring really quick, and the keyboard-mashing defence mechanic is super lame. First-Aid.  Bad mechanic. Unintuitive. It was much more user-friendly before. I could really get into it and nitpick, but those are the most frustrating issues with the survival aspect.  "Oh, that's not so bad!" you say?  Well it isn't.  I think those things could be fixed.  And may even be fixed in the future.  And even despite these issues, I really enjoy sandbox mode.  I like that I can sink a bunch of hours into a character, become really invested in them over the course of weeks, only to make some stupid, miniscule mistake and unceremoniously die.  That feels super real to me. So why the thumbs down? Two words: STORY MODE. Holy mother of god the story mode of this game is ♥♥♥♥ing horrible.  This is the videogame equivalent of The Room.  The most amateur writing I have ever experienced.  At least with The Room it's funny.  This is not.  It's cringey.  I've never rolled my eyes so much.  I want to give contructive feedback, but god ♥♥♥♥in DAMN.  Seriously, get an editor. Please. Get. An. Editor. I think maybe an alien wrote this - something that doesn't understand human logic and emotion, because the dialogue totally illogical, melodramatic, lacking motivation... Characters feel completely undeveloped and say things that don't make any sense in the context of the conversation.  Everytime a dialogue sequence occurs I have to take my headphones off and go do something else until it's over.   Every character is some goofy trope, which totally goes against the atmosphere of the rest of the game.  Why is Gimli the dwarf in this♥♥♥♥♥♥?  Why does the old woman have a cloth over her eyes??  Have you ever met a blind person??  Have you ever met a person?? The whole 'doing missions for people in order to progress' mechanic.  After the first person you encounter, (the old crone - ooo someone read Joseph Campbell...), the whole bit of running errands for people gets super stale.  The part about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ old bear who APPEARS IN FRONT OF THE DOOR as soon as the mission starts and then, since Gimli gives you all this bad advice on how to kill it, you have to just get mauled a million ♥♥♥♥ing times until you can unload enough rounds into it... And that's the way you're supposed to do it.  The whole thing is just so poorly and hastily hashed together - it really feels like a pre-release version (which is what I thought it was when I first started into it - I actually thought it was placeholder dialogue and animations). Additionally, there are absolutely no segues into story sequences.  When Gimli gets attacked by the bear, it's just suddenly happening.  I thought the game was playing the wrong sequence or something since there was no transition from gameplay into cutscene.  Likewise when you're in the dam and the convict(?) appears.  I walked into a room and suddenly I was hurt.  But there was no cue.  No audio, no animation...  No context to tell you what was going on.  Which might actually work to the story's advantage if the game was more polished.  And then you're in another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue scene.  (Seriously - to the writer of this stuff: you REALLY needed to workshop this script before it got locked down). One last thing - to the developers.  Ya'll, if you're going to make something regional, you've got to respect the region.  You've taken a lot of inspiration from the Island for sure, but you fail to express it in any sort of nuanced way.  In sandbox, it felt pretty good - rooted enough to be interesting, but abstracted enough not to feel forced.  Now that I've experienced story mode though... damn...  I'm not even going to get into that... In conclusion: The sandbox mode is great.  It's meditative.  You'll play for hours planning out your next moves, stashing gear, exploring, contemplating, wandering from town to town looting.  And then suddenly you'll make a mistake, get stuck in a storm, attacked by a wolf, or whatever and you'll have to think fast or die.  I love that.  So play the sandbox and the challenges and enjoy them.  But do not go near the story mode.  It will ruin the entire experience.

text: As most I started playing the game when it went free to play. I was very interested in playing an mmo in the universe created by Tolkien. At first the game may not seem attractive due to the outdated graphics, the clunky combat and the somewhat repetitive questing. However, if you invest a good amount of time to understand it the game starts showing its jewels. As you progress through the areas you will feel your character getting stronger, becoming a seasoned warrior whose path is tied with that of the Fellowship. The main story line not only lets you experience the Lord of the Rings trilogy to its depth but also gives you an insight on secondary plotlines that were in the background of both the books and the movies. A major advantage of the game is that it literally lets you get every part of the premium content by grinding. You can get every expansion, dungeon, skirmish e.t.c. by doing the abundant deeds spread out through all the areas. I have never seen something similar in other similar MMOs. Another great aspect of the game which adds to its immersion is the community. Everyone is very helpful to each other, bad game practices are non-existant making you feel like a member of a large fellowship. Overall, I believe people who like me are fans of the universe Tolkien created would adore this game as its huge content lets you experience the history of the books as if you were there.

text: This game has a great concept. You play as a cheesy parody of a famed action hero. The game plays as a side-scrolling, 2D platformer. You can customize your character with weapons and clothing. It's like Smash Bros., but with more death. So it's fun, the controls are good, and the graphics are nice. There's just one problem: The game is online-only. If you can't find a match, you can't play. Sorry. The only single-player content is a training tutorial. This wouldn't be a problem if the game was popular... but it isn't. You won't find a match often. When you do, it'll be against fanatics of the game. I think the worst thing is a lack of content in the game. You are forced to grind until you unlock other characters. This takes a long time due to your progress being performance-based, and the difficulty in finding a match. Which would be fine if there was some variety to the game... but there isn't. The amount of content is what you would expect from a $1 - $3 smart phone game.
